checks: In standard simplex coordinates the minimum coordinate offsets and maximal coordinate sum give a+rT with r≥0. The radius is zero exactly when all points have every coordinate at its minimum.
Each of the specified facet offsets is an actual support value of the envelope, also at radius zero. Addition of parallel translates and nonnegative homotheties adds these offsets.

Taking supports in every fixed normal proves the preserved inclusions. Grouping repeated lifted base points verifies actual fibers. If the original base set is the full integer projection, convexity of the original real projection precludes an extra integer point in conv(I).
This matches the scope of ae6af582a4950210 opening and §1, including degenerate singleton envelopes.

overlap.comparison: That theorem states the actual-fiber compatibility equivalence and gives critical caps. It does not show that this common envelope operation preserves the inclusion.
The simultaneous-facet theorem starts with positive simplex fibers already in a common orientation and does not construct envelopes for arbitrary compatible convex fibers.

readability: The hypotheses and the proof use the same scope.
review_method: Independent cold read of the exact frozen candidate, followed by source, hypothesis, overlap and arithmetic checks.
summary: Support offsets in a common simplex orientation preserve all sampled Minkowski inclusions and give the exact lifted integer fibers.
